title: Why Space Is Silent
post_description: A spacecraft can explode on screen with a huge bang—but real space is silent. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://science.nasa.gov/ems/02_anatomy/ https://howthingsfly.si.edu/ask-an-explainer/what-speed-sound-space #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Sound is a vibration that travels through a material such as air, water or metal. In the near-vacuum of space, there are far too few particles to carry an ordinary sound wave from one place to another. Light is different: it is an electromagnetic wave and does not need air or another material to travel. So a real explosion in open space would not reach a nearby observer as a movie-style boom. Inside a spacecraft, sound can travel through the cabin air.

sources.title: Anatomy of an Electromagnetic Wave
sources.supports: NASA explains that sound waves cannot travel through vacuum because there is no medium to transmit mechanical waves, while electromagnetic waves can.
